name: Suki vs Nuance DAX
title: Suki vs Nuance DAX: AI Scribe Comparison for Healthcare (2026)
description: Compare Suki AI and Nuance DAX Copilot for medical documentation. See differences in pricing, EHR integration, voice commands, and which AI scribe is best for your practice.

summary.bottom_line: Suki offers voice commands plus ambient AI documentation with strong Epic/Cerner integration—best for multi-provider environments wanting hands-free workflows. Nuance DAX Copilot (backed by Microsoft) has the deepest EHR integrations and industry-leading ambient AI but requires enterprise procurement. Both are enterprise-tier solutions requiring sales conversations.

sections.heading: Suki vs Nuance DAX: Overview
sections.content: Suki AI and Nuance DAX Copilot are enterprise-tier AI documentation solutions with different approaches. Suki combines voice commands with ambient AI—you can ask Suki to retrieve patient information, create orders, and generate notes hands-free. Nuance DAX (now owned by Microsoft) is a pure ambient AI scribe that listens to patient encounters and auto-generates documentation. Both integrate with major EHRs and require enterprise sales conversations.

sections.heading: Voice Commands vs Pure Ambient
sections.content: The key architectural difference: Suki is a voice assistant that also does ambient documentation. Beyond note generation, you can use voice commands to retrieve patient info, create orders, generate referral letters, and manage tasks during packed clinic days. This hands-free workflow management appeals to high-volume providers. DAX focuses purely on ambient documentation—listening to encounters and generating notes—without the broader voice assistant capabilities.

sections.heading: EHR Integration
sections.content: Nuance DAX has the deepest EHR integrations, particularly with Epic, thanks to Microsoft's resources and long-standing healthcare relationships. Notes flow directly into the EHR with minimal friction. Suki also has strong Epic and Cerner integrations but setup typically requires more IT coordination. Both work within existing EHR workflows rather than requiring copy/paste like lighter-weight solutions.

sections.heading: Pricing & Procurement
sections.content: Neither has transparent self-service pricing—both require sales conversations. Suki is typically quoted at $299-399/provider/month for enterprise deployments. Nuance DAX is generally higher, reflecting Microsoft enterprise pricing and deeper integration. Both require organizational commitment and IT support for implementation. These aren't solutions for solo practitioners.

recommendations.when: You want voice commands beyond just documentation (orders, lookups, referrals), you're in a multi-provider environment using Epic or Cerner, you want hands-free workflow management, or your organization isn't ready for full Microsoft enterprise procurement

You're a large health system wanting the deepest EHR integration, you prioritize pure ambient documentation over voice commands, you already have Microsoft/Nuance relationships, or you have enterprise IT resources for implementation
You're a solo/small practice—Freed, Nabla, or Mentalyc offer self-service ambient AI at $39-119/month without enterprise procurement

faqs.q: What's the main difference between Suki and Nuance DAX?
faqs.a: Suki is a voice assistant that also does ambient AI documentation—you can use voice commands for orders, lookups, and referrals beyond just note generation. Nuance DAX is a pure ambient AI scribe focused specifically on listening to encounters and generating documentation. DAX has deeper EHR integration through Microsoft's resources.

faqs.q: How much do Suki and Nuance DAX cost?
faqs.a: Both require enterprise sales conversations. Suki is typically $299-399/provider/month. Nuance DAX is generally higher with Microsoft enterprise pricing. Neither offers self-service signup—these are organizational purchases requiring IT support.

faqs.q: Do Suki and Nuance DAX work with Epic?
faqs.a: Yes, both integrate with Epic. Nuance DAX has the deepest Epic integration due to Microsoft's healthcare relationships. Suki also has strong Epic support but may require more IT coordination during setup.

faqs.q: Are there cheaper alternatives to Suki and Nuance DAX?
faqs.a: Yes. For solo practitioners and small practices, lighter-weight ambient AI scribes like Freed ($39-119/month), Nabla, and Mentalyc offer self-service signup without enterprise procurement. They work via copy/paste rather than deep EHR integration but cost a fraction of enterprise solutions.
